fields.purpose: Defines the AMBA AXI/ACE on-chip bus protocols for high-performance, high-frequency master-slave communication, suitable for high-bandwidth and low-latency designs, memory controllers, and a wide range of components. Backward compatible with AHB and APB.
key_features: Unaligned data transfers via byte strobes
Burst-based transactions with only start address issued
Separate read and write data channels (low-cost DMA)
Easy register stage addition for timing closure
Backward compatible with AHB and APB
supported_interconnect_topologies: Shared address buses and multiple data buses
Multilayer, with multiple address and data buses
fields.endianness: byte-invariant; both little-endian and big-endian components can coexist in a single memory space
fields.burst_boundary_rule: A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary
fields.intended_audience: Hardware and software engineers familiar with AMBA who want to design AXI-compatible systems and modules
fields.vendor: Arm Limited, Company 02557590 registered in England, 110 Fulbourn Road, Cambridge, England CB1 9NJ
fields.package_info_rationale: AXI is a bus protocol specification, not a packaged IC. No package/pinout/electrical-DC data exists in this document.
fields.electrical_specs_rationale: Protocol spec defines only logical signal semantics (synchronous, sampled on rising edge of ACLK, ARESETn active-LOW). No voltage/current/IO-standard information.

evidence.quote: AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification. Copyright (c) 2003-2020 Arm Limited or its affiliates. ARM IHI 0022H (ID040120)
31 March 2020 | H | Non-Confidential | EAC-0 release of version H. New optional features defined for AMBA 5 interface variants.

The AMBA 3 AXI protocol release is referred to as AXI3. The AMBA 4 AXI protocol releases are referred to as AXI4 and AXI4-Lite. The AMBA 5 AXI protocol releases are referred to as AXI5 and AXI5-Lite. The AMBA 4 ACE protocol releases are referred to as ACE and ACE-Lite. The AMBA 5 ACE protocol releases are referred to as: ACE5, ACE5-Lite, ACE5-LiteDVM, ACE5-LiteACP.

The AMBA AXI protocol supports high-performance, high-frequency system designs ... It is suitable for high-bandwidth and low-latency designs ... Separate address/control and data phases ... Support for unaligned data transfers, using byte strobes ... Uses burst-based transactions with only the start address issued ... Separate read and write data channels, that can provide low-cost Direct Memory Access (DMA) ... Support for issuing multiple outstanding addresses ... Support for out-of-order transaction completion ... Permits easy addition of register stages to provide timing closure ... It is backward-compatible with AHB and APB interfaces.
The AXI protocol is burst-based and defines five independent transaction channels: Read address (AR), Read data (R), Write address (AW), Write data (W), Write response (B).

evidence.spec_section: A1.2.1 Channel definition / Read data channel
evidence.quote: The data bus, which can be 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, or 1024 bits wide.
Most systems use one of three interconnect topologies: Shared address and data buses; Shared address buses and multiple data buses; Multilayer, with multiple address and data buses.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary.
AXI3 supports burst lengths of 1-16 transfers, for all burst types. AXI4 extends burst length support for the INCR burst type to 1-256 transfers.
